title: Verifier‑Assisted versus One‑Shot LLM Intent→Configuration: A Paired NetOpsTraceBench Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed NetOpsTraceBench, a paired comparison of a one‑shot LLM intent→configuration pipeline and a verifier‑assisted generate–validate–repair pipeline on 1,200 intent→config episodes. Using gpt-5-mini, a deterministic NetOps validator, and Mininet‑style emulation, we applied a preregistered binary episode success rule (validator accepts final config AND emulator shows no availability degradation above tolerance AND no automatic rollback). Of 1,200 planned paired tasks we completed 1,199 pairs. Baseline success = 1,196/1,199 (0.9974979149); guarded success = 1,199/1,199 (1.0000000000). The paired‑success‑rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0025020851 (95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.0000, 0.0058381985], bootstrap_seed=1729, resamples=10,000); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. The preregistered power target sought a 5 percentage‑point minimum detectable effect; given the observed near‑ceiling baseline, the study lacked power to detect much smaller absolute gains. Representative validator traces and provider audit logs show repair was invoked only three times. Under these controlled emulation and task‑corpus conditions we find no statistically significant advantage for the verifier‑assisted pipeline; we report artifacts, analytic deviation (Wilcoxon → exact McNemar for binary outcomes), and detailed execution accounting to support reproducible interpretation.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent expressed in natural language into executable device configurations for network operations (NetOps). Systems and survey literature emphasize that operational reliability depends on the orchestration and assurance stack (model + verifier + provenance + sandboxed execution) rather than on an LLM alone. Generate–validate–repair (verifier‑assisted) architectures are a canonical mitigation strategy: an LLM proposes candidate outputs, an automated verifier checks constraints and safety, and an automated repair loop iterates until constraints are satisfied. Despite conceptual support, publicly archived, preregistered, paired evidence measuring whether verifier assistance yields an operationally meaningful improvement (rollback‑aware binary success) relative to one‑shot generation remains limited.

We address this gap with NetOpsTraceBench: a preregistered, paired, emulator‑grounded study comparing (A) baseline one‑shot NL→config generation and (B) a guarded generate–validate–repair pipeline using the same shared initial candidate per pair. Research question (preregistered): Can a reproducible, workflow‑centered benchmark of paired intent→config episodes produce an objective paired binary success metric that reliably distinguishes verifier‑assisted pipelines from one‑shot generation across two simulated topologies? Our contributions: (1) a preregistered experimental design and full execution artifacts (study ID rX4f7-1); (2) a paired analysis on 1,199 completed pairs using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic validator; (3) explicit disclosure of a preregistered subgroup hypothesis (H3, topology‑cluster breakdown) that was not executed as a confirmatory subgroup analysis and explanation of that omission; and (4) archived artifacts and deterministic traces enabling exact reproduction of the reported aggregate analysis.
sections.related_work: Recent surveys and systems work position LLMs as components within larger AIOps/NetOps workflows and repeatedly stress that correctness and trustworthiness are emergent properties of the whole stack rather than of the model alone. Prior generate–validate‑repair proposals (NL→formal specs, topology compilers, RAG firewalls, and configuration detectors) demonstrate feasibility of verifier‑guided repair in constrained settings but show sensitivity to task selection and verifier strictness. Empirical studies catalogue LLM failure modes relevant to executable artifacts—hallucination, semantic/unit errors, overconfidence/miscalibration, and prompt‑injection vulnerability—motivating external verifier scaffolding. Surveys call for workflow‑centered benchmarks that record full provider and validator traces, embed emulator execution to check operational side effects (availability/rollback), and preregister analysis choices to reduce researcher degrees of freedom. NetOpsTraceBench operationalizes those recommendations by preregistering seeds, inclusion/exclusion rules, a binary rollback‑aware episode success metric, and by archiving raw model outputs, validator traces, and execution manifests for reproducible analysis.
sections.methodology:
Design and preregistration: The study was preregistered (study_id = rX4f7-1; preregistration manifest SHA‑256 = 77abe8b493bde44484e0b3d02cfd7f9ec1621ff7e7847889082ae177a7ed5712) and froze hypotheses, inclusion/exclusion rules, contamination thresholds, seeds, stopping rules, and the planned paired analysis. The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The preregistered power plan targeted an absolute paired increase of 5 percentage points (MDE = 0.05) at α=0.05 and 80% power under baseline≈0.70 assumptions.

Task corpus, topology clusters, and contamination: The benchmark scope defined 1,200 deterministic tasks split into two simulated topology clusters (edge=600, core=600). Tasks are generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 with frozen per‑task seeds; payloads include initial_state, expected_final_state, explicit required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, workflow_policies, and declared difficulty labels. Contamination detection was preregistered (token/subsequence overlap threshold T_contam = 0.85; optional embedding similarity threshold 0.92); flagged pairs would be excluded automatically. The missingness plan and exclusion rules were frozen prior to execution.

Paired pipeline semantics and shared_initial_candidate rationale: To isolate verifier and repair effects, we used a shared_initial_candidate design: for each task a single LLM initial candidate was generated and used for both conditions (baseline one‑shot and guarded verifier‑assisted). This choice controls generation variability between paired episodes so that observed differences arise from validator and repair stages rather than from independent sampling variability in LLM outputs. Per preregistration maximums, initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1 and maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; retrieval‑augmentation was disabled. Model requests recorded requested_model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json) and the orchestration adapter was hosted_netops_gvr_v1.

Baseline and guarded implementations: Baseline (one‑shot) recorded the shared initial candidate and proceeded to deterministic parsing and emulator preflight checks without invoking repair. Guarded fed the shared_initial_candidate to deterministic_netops_validator_v5; acceptance triggered emulator execution, rejection could trigger a single automated repair LLM call per the frozen retry policy. The validator enforces workflow_policies and emits structured diagnostics (parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, validation_after.valid, repair_applied).

Deterministic validation, emulation, and primary success rule: Episodes were scored by deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and executed in a Mininet‑style emulator to detect availability degradation and automatic rollback events. The preregistered binary episode success required (1) validator acceptance of the final configuration (validation_after.valid == true), (2) emulator execution showing no availability degradation above the preregistered tolerance, and (3) no automatic rollback during simulated execution. All raw model outputs, provider traces, validator traces, and execution logs were archived.

Analysis executor and analytic deviation: The preregistration specified a nonparametric paired test and bootstrap CI computation using paired_binary_analysis_v1. Because outcomes are binary and concentrated in concordant cells, the archived confirmatory analysis executed an exact McNemar two‑sided test for paired binary outcomes and computed a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI with frozen bootstrap_seed = 1729 and 10,000 resamples. This analytic choice (exact McNemar for binary paired outcomes) is documented and archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; analysis/results.json; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl).
sections.results:
Execution and accounting: Execution started 2026-08-30T01:21:55.415955+00:00 and completed 2026-08-30T03:15:12.141890+00:00. Planned episodes = 2,400; completed episodes = 2,398; failed_episode_count = 2; complete_pair_count = 1,199. Provider audit: hosted_model_call_event_count = 1,203; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 1,202; stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 1,200; repair = 3. Representative per‑episode scoring artifacts and validator traces are archived (examples: execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json). The aggregated condition summary is stored in analysis/condition_summary.csv.

Primary confirmatory outcomes: The paired 2×2 contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is n11 = 1,196, n10 = 3, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Baseline_success_count = 1,196/1,199 (0.9974979149291076); guarded_success_count = 1,199/1,199 (1.0); paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002502085070892446. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10,000) = [0.0000, 0.005838198498748957]. All numbers and bootstrap parameters are archived (analysis/results.json; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl).

Missingness, contamination, and repairs: analysis/missingness_summary.csv reports complete_pairs = 1,199; failed_baseline_episodes = 1; failed_guarded_episodes = 1; both_missing_pairs = 1. analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty (no automatic contamination exclusions). Repair invocation was rare: repair = 3 across 1,200 shared initial generations, matching repair_provider traces present for exactly three episodes (execution/provider_calls/*). Validator traces typically record validation_after.valid = true and repair_applied = false, explaining the low repair count.

Preregistered topology‑cluster breakdown (H3): The preregistration included hypothesis H3 (confirmatory: paired difference consistent across two simulated topology clusters: edge vs core). The archived confirmatory analysis artifacts do not contain per‑cluster inferential results: the confirmatory test was executed on the aggregated paired sample and only aggregate contingency and CI artifacts were archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; analysis/results.json). Therefore H3 was not executed as a confirmatory subgroup analysis in the archived run. The absence of archived per‑cluster contingency tables or per‑cluster inferential outputs means H3 remains untested in the confirmatory sense; exploratory per‑cluster breakdowns could be computed from the raw scoring artifacts but were not performed as part of the preregistered confirmatory analysis and are not reported here to avoid post‑hoc confirmation. Readers can reproduce per‑cluster summaries from archived per‑episode scoring artifacts (execution/scoring/*.json and execution/task_manifest.jsonl) if desired.

Representative artifacts: Representative task manifests and scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/task-00000X-*.json) illustrate heterogeneous declared difficulty levels and validator diagnostics; they also show that the shared_initial_candidate often satisfied deterministic validator checks, producing validation_after.valid = true without repair. Aggregate artifacts referenced above contain the exact numbers reported here.
sections.discussion:
Statistical interpretation: The exact McNemar p = 0.25 and bootstrap CI that includes zero indicate no statistically significant advantage for the guarded pipeline under the chosen corpus and validator settings. Two artifact‑grounded explanations are supported. First, the baseline one‑shot success rate was near ceiling (≈99.75%), leaving limited absolute headroom for improvement; the preregistered MDE (5 percentage points) assumed a much lower baseline and therefore the achieved sample is underpowered to detect the observed ≈0.25 percentage‑point effect. Second, design choices materially reduced repair invocation: the deterministic task generator produced clear required sequences and the deterministic validator accepted most shared initial candidates, so the repair stage was seldom exercised (repair = 3). Both points are observable in the archived task manifests, validator traces, and provider audit logs.

Operational implications and recommendations: When initial generation already satisfies verifier constraints for well‑specified synthetic tasks, verifier scaffolding will be infrequently exercised and measured gains on a binary success metric will be small. To evaluate verifier value in practice, future benchmarks should (a) increase task ambiguity/adversariality, (b) vary verifier strictness and rule sets, (c) test multiple LLM families and fine‑tuned variants, and (d) predefine meaningful per‑cluster or per‑risk‑tier confirmatory analyses when subgroup effects are of primary interest. The archived artifacts here permit exact replay and principled sensitivity studies to explore these directions.

Threats to validity: Internal validity is strong due to deterministic task generation and frozen seeds; construct validity depends on whether the preregistered binary success metric maps to operational correctness across production environments. External validity is limited by (i) a single requested model family (gpt-5-mini), (ii) synthetic/consented vendor‑agnostic tasks, and (iii) Mininet‑style emulation that may not capture vendor idiosyncrasies or routing convergence phenomena. Conclusion validity is constrained by the low number of discordant pairs (n10+n01 = 3) which reduces resolution for small absolute effects. These limitations are documented in the archived preregistration and in analysis artifacts.
sections.conclusion: NetOpsTraceBench executed a preregistered paired benchmark comparing one‑shot and verifier‑assisted NL→config pipelines on 1,199 completed pairs using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic validator. Under the chosen synthetic task corpus and validator configuration, baseline one‑shot generation achieved near‑ceiling success (≈99.75%); guarded increased absolute success by ≈0.25 percentage points but this effect was not statistically significant (exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25, 95% bootstrap CI includes zero). Archived execution manifests, provider audits (model_calls_used = 1,203; repairs invoked = 3), validator traces, and analysis artifacts support the interpretation that the null result reflects limited headroom given task and verifier choices rather than a general refutation of verifier utility. The run archives full artifacts and seeds to enable reproducible follow‑up sensitivity studies that vary corpus adversariality, verifier strictness, models, and predefined subgroup analyses (including the preregistered topology‑cluster breakdown H3, which was not executed as a confirmatory subgroup test in this run).

limitations: Single model family tested (gpt-5-mini); results do not imply generality across other LLMs or fine‑tuned variants.
Task corpus skew: synthetic/consented tasks yielded near‑ceiling baseline success (≈99.75%), limiting headroom and statistical power to detect practical improvements by guarded pipelines.

Emulator fidelity: Mininet‑style emulation and deterministic validators approximate production behavior but may not capture all deployment failure modes (routing convergence, vendor idiosyncrasies, transient telemetry).

Verifier configuration dependence: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 acceptance thresholds and parsing rules materially affect outcomes; different verifier strictness could change repair invocation rates and measured gains.

Analytic deviation documented: the preregistration specified a Wilcoxon signed‑rank paired procedure; the archived confirmatory analysis used an exact McNemar test because outcomes were binary. This deviation is recorded in the archived analysis artifacts and in the Disclosure Statement above.
Operational external validity: absence of heterogeneous vendor renderers, real production templates, and live rollouts constrain direct production generalization.
